sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:8

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:8:1
items.html: When ABYA are in wholeness: This speaks of the time when Beria, Yetzira and Assiya are in wholeness, when they ascend to Atzilut, such as on Shabbat, when they clothe one another, like the upper man who is soul and body and garment and sits in the palace of the King.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:8:2
items.html: Head, arms, body, palace: These are names for the ten Sefirot of the Partzuf: the head is the Sefira of Keter within it. The arms are Hesed and Gevura: the Sefira of Hesed is the right arm, and the Sefira of Gevura is the left arm. The body is the Sefira of Tifferet, and from the navel downward are the four Sefirot, Netzah, Hod, Yesod and Malchut.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:8:3
items.html: The ten Sefirot of the body are called ten measures: This refers back to what he wrote above (Chapter 5, Item 1), that Hochma is soul, Bina is body, ZA is garment, and Malchut is palace. And it has already been clarified that on the side of the light there is no limit at all, and moreover it does not even mind the limit that is in the vessels, since it therefore performs a striking (as above, Chapter 1, Item 70, in the Ohr Pnimi); and the vessels that impose a limit begin, among the ten Sefirot, only from Bina downward, namely: body, garment, palace, which are phase two, phase three and phase four; but phase one, which is Hochma, called soul, is not considered a vessel at all, and this is what the ARI writes, that since the ten Sefirot of the body are called ten measures, because from phase two the vessels that create limit and measure begin, whereas the ten Sefirot of the soul, namely phase one, called Hochma, "have no measure at all," because phase one is not considered coarseness at all, as written in the Ohr Pnimi mentioned above, and therefore it has no phase of vessel or measure.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:8:4
items.html: This is garment: This is garment.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:8:5
items.html: With respect to Keter, called Ein Sof: That is, with respect to Keter, called Ein Sof, even Hochma, which has coarseness in it, is regarded so, because in Ein Sof there is nothing at all of the will to receive, as clarified at length above (Ohr Pnimi, Part 1, Chapter 1, Item 50, Sub Header, "And the reason"), and therefore it is called by the name phase one.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:8:6
items.html: Even in Keter these four phases are discerned: As written above, that even in Keter the four phases called soul, body, garment, palace are discerned, which are Hochma and Bina, Tifferet and Malchut (HB TM), but only in the phase of roots.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:8:7
items.html:
The conclusion of the degrees, wherever it is: The conclusion of the degrees, wherever it is, comes about only by cause of the screen that is in the vessel of Malchut within them, as has been well clarified in the previous parts, in such a way that the expansion of the degrees from Ein Sof, blessed be He, to the emanated being is found to stop and remain "standing," ceasing to expand, at the moment it touches the screen — like one standing on the ground above it, where the ground does not allow him to expand within it and inside it; so does the screen halt the light from expanding within it and inside it, and therefore the screen is called by the name "ground."
And it has already been clarified above, in the Ohr Pnimi (Part 3, Chapter 3, Item 6), that the ten Sefirot of the world of Beria were created by the refinement of the screen of phase three, which is in the world of Atzilut, to phase two — see there (and see the Inner Observation, Part 2, Item 72, Sub Header, "And so that" — see there the whole passage) — and this is what is written, that by way of the screen, which is the ground of the palace of Atzilut, it shone downward, and so on, that is, by cause of its refinement, as clarified there.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:8:8
items.html: Like a seal and its imprint: That is, just as the seal lacks nothing of all the forms found in the seal, so all the forms found in the world of Atzilut emerge in the world of Beria; and for this reason this is called by the name seal and imprint. And there is a further and more original reason, for the whole coming of the upper light to Beria is by force of that same ascending reflected light, which by the coupling of striking upon the screen of phase two that is in the ground of Atzilut, above it, in Atzilut itself — that very same reflected light returned and sparkled and passed through the screen and widened the vessel of Malchut into ten Sefirot from itself and within itself, and expanded there from above downward (as has been well clarified above in the Ohr Pnimi, Part 3, Chapter 2, Item 3); so that it is found that all the phases that the reflected light clothed in Atzilut from the ground upward, returned and were drawn and came also from the ground downward. And this reflected light is entirely like a seal, in that whatever is engraved on it is found to be copied onto the imprint made from it; so that reflected light, all the phases and the whole stature that it clothed from below upward, returned and brought them to Beria from above downward, and copied them there in Beria without any lack or change whatsoever, and therefore this action is called by the name seal and imprint.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:8:9
items.html: The general rule: This is the general rule: wherever it is discerned that the reflected light ascends from below upward, the self of the upper light is found clothed there in this reflected light, which indicates the expansion of the light of Ein Sof, blessed be He, to make vessels, of which the ARI speaks above (Part 1, Chapter 1, Item 1); but in the place where it is discerned that the reflected light expands from above downward, in the manner mentioned, in the ten Sefirot of Beria, as written above in the passage nearby, then the upper light clothed here in this reflected light is no longer the self of the upper light, but is regarded rather as "a light of offspring," drawn from the upper light, "and not the very light of the upper light itself." And the reason is that it is drawn by force of the screen that raises reflected light because of the restraint within it, as above, and therefore the power of the lower one is already mixed into it, and it too is limited by the measure of the vessels and the stature that is in the screen, since the screen precedes the expansion of these ten Sefirot; that is, the screen is the cause that brings about the appearance of these ten Sefirot, and for this reason the light is limited by it, and it has already gone out from the category of the self of the upper light and is regarded as a light of offspring — unlike the reflected light ascending from the screen upward, which cannot raise anything at all of its coarseness there (as above, Part 3, Chapter 4, Ohr Pnimi, Item 50) — see there. Indeed this is said of the world of Beria and below; but in Atzilut there is no screen at all, as above, and therefore every light that is there, up to the conclusion of the legs, is regarded as the self of the light.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:8:10
items.html: For the Malchut of the upper one is for this reason called a spark of the Creator, as above, being what draws and emanates the degree below her — as written above, that all the degrees and the Partzufim [pl. of Partzuf] and the worlds, from the Rosh [head] of the line to the end of Assiya, emerge and are emanated one from the other by way of cause and effect. That is, that the Malchut of Malchut of every upper one descends below her degree, and she is what draws all four phases of the lower one, as is explained well and at length in Part 2, in the Inner Observation, Chapter 5, item 59. (For all these matters would have needed to be written here, had I not spared the printing costs.)
